prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The time to vote Green is now. In an age of climate chaos, a broken democracy and the divisive threat of Brexit, only the Greens offer a fast, fair transformation that lifts everyone up.

Our Green New Deal is a ten‑year plan to put the UK on track to net‑zero by 2030 while tackling inequality. We will invest over £100bn a year (plus UBI) to create millions of secure green jobs and a safer, fairer future.

- Energy: Replace fossil fuels with UK renewables, with wind supplying around 70% of electricity by 2030. End oil and gas subsidies, ban fracking forever, prohibit new nuclear, expand storage and the grid, and connect to European clean power. A rising Carbon Tax will make fossil fuels unviable as renewables soar.

- Housing: Insulate every home by 2030; deep‑retrofit 1m homes a year; build 100,000 energy‑efficient council homes annually; roll out rooftop solar to 10m homes; switch to clean heat and heat networks; require A‑rated rented homes; plan car‑free, people‑first neighbourhoods.

- Transport: Make public transport cheaper than driving; electrify rail and expand capacity; bring rail into public ownership; give councils control of buses; invest £2.5bn/year in walking and cycling; end new roads and runways; introduce a Frequent Flyer Levy and ban flight ads; end sales of new petrol/diesel vehicles by 2030 and build a national EV charging network; 20mph default on residential streets.

- Industry: Rebuild UK manufacturing around clean tech; fund R&D and grants to decarbonise; create regional mutual banks; establish a right to repair, 10‑year product warranties and circular economy rules; cut fluorinated gases; start CCS for steel/cement; a just transition from oil/coal with £2bn/year for skills.

- Food, farming & forestry: Shift subsidies to agroecology and mixed farming; plant 700m trees; restore hedgerows and habitats; halve pesticide use and ban the worst chemicals; expand agroforestry to 50% of farms by 2030; rewild where possible; uphold a right to food; reduce floods with nature‑based solutions.

- Incomes: Phase in a Universal Basic Income so no one is worse off (adult £89/week; pensioners £178/week; supplements for children, disabled people, carers). Raise the Living Wage to £12; 35 hours/week free childcare from 9 months; rent controls and an end to no‑fault evictions; move toward a four‑day week with no loss of pay.

- Democracy and Europe: A People’s Vote with Remain on the ballot; transform the EU to deliver climate and social justice; replace First Past the Post with proportional voting; an elected second chamber; votes at 16; citizens’ assemblies and devolution; a Carbon Chancellor and a Future Generations Act at the heart of government.

- Public services: Reverse austerity; boost the NHS by at least £6bn/year (rising), end privatisation and prioritise mental health; free home social care for over‑65s; add £4bn/year for schools, scrap tuition fees and write off £9k‑era student debt; restore arts and climate education; expand adult learning.

- Justice, rights, equality: End the hostile environment; humane, rights‑based migration; make misogyny a hate crime; strengthen LGBTIQA+ and disability rights; halve the prison population with prevention and restorative justice; end the war on drugs with legal, regulated control.

- Nature & animals: An ecocide law; stronger land and sea protections (at least 30% of UK waters fully protected by 2030); a new right to roam; end factory farming, live exports and hunting; enshrine animal sentience.

Paying for it: A fair tax revolution—Carbon Tax; merge income/wealth taxes to close loopholes; raise Corporation Tax to 24%; crack down on avoidance; replace Council Tax and Business Rates with a Land Value Tax; end wasteful spending (Trident, HS2, road‑building, airport expansion); and borrow for green capital while rates are low, crowding in private investment.

The choices we make now matter like never before. Every Green vote is a vote to tackle the Climate Emergency, renew democracy and deliver social justice. If not now, then when?
